title: A finite unramified morphism with one purely inseparable fibre point is locally a closed immersion
statement: Let $\pi:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $s\in S$, and let $x\in X$ be the unique point of the underlying topological fibre $\pi^{-1}(s)$, equivalently the unique point of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Assume that $\pi$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism], and that the residue-field extension $\kappa(s)\subseteq\kappa(x)$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that the restricted morphism $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. (Stacks Project, Tag [04DG].)

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04DG (label lemma-finite-unramified-one-point), statement and proof at lines 706-743

proof.text: Reduction to an affine base. Choose an affine open $V\subseteq S$ containing $s$ and write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with $s$ the prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$. Since $\pi$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], $\pi^{-1}(V)$ is affine, $\pi^{-1}(V)=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and the ring map $\varphi:A\to B$ inducing $\pi|_{\pi^{-1}(V)}$ makes $B$ a finitely generated $A$-module. The points of $\pi^{-1}(s)\subseteq\pi^{-1}(V)$ are the primes $\mathfrak q'\subset B$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')=\mathfrak p$; by hypothesis there is exactly one, $\mathfrak q$, corresponding to $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-residue-field-identification] (applied to $A$ and to $B$, compatibly with $\varphi$) the residue fields of the schemes are $\kappa(s)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)=A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\kappa(x)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)=B_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qB_{\mathfrak q}$, and the map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ of [def-weil-residue-field] becomes the map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ induced by $\varphi$; so $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. It suffices to find $f\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that $\pi^{-1}(D(f))\to D(f)$ is a closed immersion, $D(f)\subseteq V$ being an open neighbourhood of $s$ in $S$.

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04DG, proof, lines 727-733 ('The question is local on S. Hence we may assume that S = Spec(A). By definition of a finite morphism this implies X = Spec(B) ... Let q be the prime corresponding to x')

proof.text: The fibre ring is a finite product of finite separable extensions. Let $F=B\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $j:B\to F$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. The restriction $\operatorname{Spec}B=\pi^{-1}(V)\to V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is unramified by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open](2), hence so is its base change along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open](1); by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] this base change is $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, induced by the structure map. By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-algebra-over-field-product] there are $n\ge0$ and finite separable algebraic field extensions $L_1,\dots,L_n$ of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $F\cong L_1\times\cdots\times L_n$ as $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebras.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00UW (algebra-lemma-unramified-at-prime), proof, algebra.tex lines 41584-41591; Morphisms, Lemma 02G7 (morphisms-lemma-unramified-over-field) part (2), morphisms.tex lines 7797-7805

proof.text: The fibre ring is a single field, isomorphic to $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-localization-quotient], $F\cong B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$ as $B$-algebras, $B_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization of $B$ at $\varphi(A\setminus\mathfrak p)$. (a) $n\ge1$: the map $B\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ kills $\varphi(\mathfrak p)\subseteq\mathfrak q$ and sends $\varphi(A\setminus\mathfrak p)\subseteq B\setminus\mathfrak q$ to units, so it factors through $B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$, which is therefore nonzero. (b) $n\le1$: for each $i$ let $Q_i=\ker(F\to L_i)$, a prime (maximal) ideal of $F$, the $Q_i$ pairwise distinct. The composite $A\to B\xrightarrow{j}F\to L_i$ equals $A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F\to L_i$, and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to L_i$ is injective (a ring map out of a field to a nonzero ring), so its kernel is $\ker(A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p))=\mathfrak p$ [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra](a); hence the prime $j^{-1}(Q_i)$ of $B$ lies over $\mathfrak p$, so $j^{-1}(Q_i)=\mathfrak q$ for every $i$ (step 1). Primes of $B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$ correspond injectively to primes of $B_{\mathfrak p}$, and these injectively to their contractions in $B$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; so $Q_i=Q_k$ for all $i,k$, i.e. $n=1$. Thus $F=L_1=:L$ is a field, finite separable algebraic over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, with unique prime $(0)$ and $j^{-1}(0)=\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-residue-field-iso] applied to $\mathfrak Q=(0)$ the induced map $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to\kappa((0))=F$ is an isomorphism; it is a map of $B$-algebras, hence of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebras by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra](c). So $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong L$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is both purely inseparable and separable algebraic.

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04DG, proof, lines 734-737 ('Conditions (2), (3) and (4) imply that B_q/pB_q = kappa(p) ... Hence we see that B_p/pB_p = kappa(p)'); the passage through B_q and Algebra Lemma 00EA (lemma-unique-prime-over-localize-below, B_q = B_p) is replaced here by the direct count of the factors of the fibre ring F = B_p/pB_p, as in the proof of Algebra Lemma 00UW (algebra.tex lines 41590-41595)

proof.text: Separable and purely inseparable forces equality: $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F$ is an isomorphism. Let $\alpha\in L=F$. In characteristic $0$, purely inseparable means $L=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. In characteristic $p>0$, $c=\alpha^{p^m}\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for some $m$, so the minimal polynomial $P_\alpha$ of $\alpha$ divides $T^{p^m}-c=(T-\alpha)^{p^m}$ in $L[T]$, hence $P_\alpha=(T-\alpha)^e$ for some $e\ge1$; as $P_\alpha$ is separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] it has no repeated root, so $e=1$ and $\alpha\in\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Hence the structure map $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F\cong B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective. (This is the footnote of 04DG: under (2), condition (4) is equivalent to $\kappa(s)=\kappa(x)$.)

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04DG, statement, footnote to condition (4), lines 715-717

proof.text: Nakayama: $A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective. $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ and residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. $M=B_{\mathfrak p}$ is a finitely generated $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module (the images $b_i/1$ of $A$-module generators $b_i$ of $B$ generate it), and $(\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p})M=\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$. By step 4 the submodule $N=\varphi_{\mathfrak p}(A_{\mathfrak p})=A_{\mathfrak p}\cdot1$ maps onto $M/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}M=B_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pB_{\mathfrak p}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], $N=M$: the ring map $\varphi_{\mathfrak p}:A_{\mathfrak p}\to B_{\mathfrak p}$ is surjective.

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04DG, proof, lines 738-740 ('As B is a finite A-module we see from Nakayama's lemma (see Algebra, Lemma 00DV) that B_p = phi(A_p)')

proof.text: Spreading out: $A_f\to B_f$ is surjective for some $f\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$. Let $Q=B/\varphi(A)$, a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. By step 5, for each $b\in B$ we have $b/1=\varphi(a)/\varphi(t)$ in $B_{\mathfrak p}$ with $a\in A$, $t\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$, so $\varphi(u)(\varphi(t)b-\varphi(a))=0$ for some $u\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$, i.e. $ut\notin\mathfrak p$ kills the class of $b$ in $Q$; hence $Q_{\mathfrak p}=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator], $\operatorname{Ann}_A(Q)\not\subseteq\mathfrak p$; choose $f\in\operatorname{Ann}_A(Q)\setminus\mathfrak p$. Then $\varphi(f)B\subseteq\varphi(A)$, and every element $b/\varphi(f)^m$ of $B_f$ equals $\varphi(f)b/\varphi(f)^{m+1}=\varphi(a)/\varphi(f)^{m+1}$ for some $a\in A$, so $\varphi_f:A_f\to B_f$ is surjective.

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04DG, proof, lines 740-742 ('Hence (using the finiteness of B as an A-module again) there exists a f in A, f not in p such that B_f = phi(A_f)')

proof.text: Conclusion. $U=D(f)\subseteq V$ is an open neighbourhood of $s$ in $S$, and $\pi^{-1}(U)=\{\mathfrak q'\subset B:\varphi(f)\notin\mathfrak q'\}=D(\varphi(f))\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}A_f\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B_f\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ are open immersions onto $U$ and $\pi^{-1}(U)$; by functoriality of $\operatorname{Spec}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] they identify $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_f):\operatorname{Spec}B_f\to\operatorname{Spec}A_f$. So $U$ and $\pi^{-1}(U)$ are affine with rings $A_f$ and $B_f$, and the ring map $\mathcal O_U(U)\to\mathcal O(\pi^{-1}(U))$ is $\varphi_f$, surjective by step 6. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-affine-cover-criterion](2), applied to $\pi|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}:\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ with the one-member affine cover $\{U\}$, this morphism is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Stacks Etale Morphisms, Lemma 04DG, proof, line 742 ('such that B_f = phi(A_f) as desired'), with Morphisms, Lemma 01QO for the closed-immersion criterion

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against Stacks 04DG (etale.tex 706-721): it is correct (the G1 statement adds only the equivalent scheme-theoretic description of the fibre point); stmt_deps kept. Wrote the 04DG proof in seven steps: affine reduction via the definition of a finite morphism and the Spec residue-field identification; the fibre ring F = B (x)_A kappa(p) is unramified over kappa(p) (base change, 02GA/02G6 node) hence a finite product of finite separable extensions (new node lem-weil-pbc-unramified-algebra-over-field-product, 02G7(1)/00UW proof); the unique point over s forces one factor, which is kappa(q) by the fibre-ring residue-field node; separable plus purely inseparable gives kappa(p) = F (elementary, the 04DG footnote); Nakayama over A_p (00DV node) gives A_p -> B_p surjective; the support/annihilator node gives f not in p with A_f -> B_f surjective; the 01QO criterion node gives the closed immersion over D(f). Departure inside the node level: Stacks passes through B_q/pB_q = kappa(p) and Algebra 00EA (B_q = B_p); here F = B_p/pB_p is computed directly, which avoids a node for 00EA. One new node (unsplit, no exact Mathlib match: the unramified product decomposition is a composite of Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_formallyUnramified_of_field and Algebra.FormallyEtale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod). Mathlib note for the item: Algebra.FormallyUnramified.range_eq_top_of_isPurelyInseparable (RingTheory/Unramified/Field.lean:161) is step 4 for fields.
